blocks.content: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935 in accordance with the provisions of the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.

rows: Governance and powers of the Central Bank
Regulation and supervision of commercial banks
Currency issuance, monetary policy, lender of last resort
Licensing of banks, branch expansion, minimum capital norms
Created RBI as a central monetary authority
Enacted post-independence to protect depositors and structure banking

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The Reserve Bank of India was established on April 1, 1935, based on the recommendations of the Hilton Young Commission (1926).
Originally established as a private shareholders' bank, the RBI was fully nationalised on January 1, 1949.
The primary legal framework governing the central bank's functions is the Reserve Bank of India Act, 1934.
Commercial banking operations, licensing, and regulation across India fall under the Banking Regulation Act, 1949.
The central office of the RBI was permanently shifted from Kolkata to Mumbai in 1937.
The Royal Commission on Indian Currency and Finance (Hilton Young Commission) is frequently tested as the body that recommended establishing the RBI.
Note the nationalisation date: January 1, 1949, enacted under the Reserve Bank (Transfer to Public Ownership) Act, 1948.
Distinguish between RBI Act 1934 (regulates the central bank) and Banking Regulation Act 1949 (regulates commercial banks).
